stories.headline: S&P 500 HOLDS GAINS, NASDAQ-100 SLIPS AS WALL STREET AWAITS BIG TECH EARNINGS
stories.body: The S&P 500 added 0.28% to 7,713 while the Nasdaq 100 eased 0.13% to 29,490, a quiet session sandwiched between Monday's 530-point Dow rally and a earnings-heavy back half of the week.
stories.explain: A cap-weighted tech index can lag a broad-market gain on a single day when just a few megacap names rotate lower even as breadth improves elsewhere, which is roughly what happened here. With the Fed's Oct. 28 decision and a wave of hyperscaler earnings both on deck, traders have little incentive to add risk aggressively today; the market is effectively marking time until those two catalysts clarify whether the AI-capex spending cycle and the rate path both stay supportive.

stories.headline: 10-YEAR YIELD EASES TO 5.12% AS TRADERS LOCK IN A FED HOLD
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield slipped 2 basis points to 5.12% ahead of next Wednesday's FOMC decision, where futures markets assign an overwhelming probability to the Fed holding its target range at 3.75%-4.00%.
stories.explain: When a rate decision is this close to fully priced, the yield curve stops moving on the decision itself and starts moving on the tone that's expected to accompany it, in this case a 'hawkish hold' that keeps a December hike or cut on the table. A government data backlog from earlier this year has also pushed the Fed toward leaning on private data like ADP payrolls instead of delayed official releases, which adds a layer of uncertainty to the dot plot that traders are already pricing into term premium at the long end.

stories.headline: WTI SLIPS TO $98 BUT HOLDS MOST OF ITS HORMUZ RISK PREMIUM
stories.body: WTI crude fell 0.55% to $98 a barrel while Brent held above $108, both still carrying a geopolitical premium tied to reported tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure.
stories.explain: A chokepoint risk premium is priced through war-risk insurance and options skew long before a single barrel actually fails to ship, so crude can stay elevated purely on the threat of disruption. The fact that WTI is pulling back only modestly, rather than round-tripping back toward pre-spike levels, tells you traders still see the Hormuz situation as unresolved rather than de-escalating, which matters directly for CPI given how quickly pump prices pass through.

stories.headline: GOLD RETREATS TO $4,148 AS THE DOLLAR FIRMS AND HAVEN DEMAND COOLS
stories.body: Spot gold fell 0.43% to roughly $4,148 an ounce as the dollar index inched down only modestly to 101.73, with the metal's pullback driven more by easing safe-haven demand than by any single dollar move.
stories.explain: Gold pays no yield, so every basis point the 10-year holds near 5.12% raises the opportunity cost of parking money in bullion instead of interest-bearing assets. With equities steady and no fresh escalation headline out of the Middle East today, some of the tactical haven bid that built up over the past two weeks is unwinding back into cash and short-duration Treasuries.

stories.headline: SPACEX'S 161% REVENUE JUMP SETS THE TONE FOR THIS WEEK'S BIG TECH GAUNTLET
stories.body: SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue up 161% year over year to $14.58 billion after the bell Monday, a number that's lifting futures sentiment into a week stacked with hyperscaler and AI-adjacent earnings that will test whether capex spending is translating into actual growth.
stories.explain: SpaceX isn't in the S&P 500, but its print functions as an early read on demand for launch, satellite broadband and the infrastructure layer that underpins a lot of the AI buildout narrative. A beat this size gives risk appetite a tailwind heading into names investors actually hold, which is why index futures ticked higher almost immediately after the number crossed the wire.

stories.headline: AP PRESEASON TOP 25 LOOMS AS FLORIDA, DUKE HEADLINE NO. 1 RACE
stories.body: With the men's regular season tipping off Nov. 2, the AP's preseason Top 25 is expected any day. Florida was tabbed No. 1 in the SEC's preseason media poll and is widely projected as Duke's closest rival for the national top spot; the two meet Dec. 1 in Gainesville as part of the ACC/SEC Challenge.

stories.headline: 2026-27 SEASON TIPS OFF AS RECORD $12.5B LAKERS SALE AWAITS LEAGUE VOTE
stories.body: The league's new season opened tonight with a three-game slate, Celtics at Pistons, 76ers at Knicks and Thunder at Spurs, while the agreed $12.5 billion sale of the Lakers to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner still needs NBA Board of Governors approval next month. Final scores from tonight's openers were not yet available at publication time.

stories.headline: TRADE DEADLINE BUILDS AS WEEK 7 LEAVES PLAYOFF PICTURE SCRAMBLED
stories.body: With the Nov. 10 trade deadline two and a half weeks out, front offices are working the phones after a Week 7 slate that saw Seattle fall 17-14 in overtime at Denver, dropping the Seahawks to 3-3 and tightening the NFC West race ahead of their Oct. 25 home date with Kansas City.

stories.headline: WEEK 7'S UPSETS RESHAPE THE PLAYOFF PICTURE HEADING INTO WEEK 8
stories.body: Last weekend's chaos, BYU's 28-24 stunner over Notre Dame, Ohio State's shaky 19-15 escape past Indiana that cost it QB Julian Sayin to injury, Florida's comeback win over Texas, and Tennessee's rout of Alabama, has scrambled the committee picture as teams turn toward Week 8.

deepDive.title: The Hawkish Hold: Why the Fed's Words Will Matter More Than Its Rate Next Week
content: Futures markets are pricing an overwhelming probability that the Fed holds its target range at 3.75%-4.00% on Oct. 28, and the 10-year sitting at 5.12% today reflects a bond market that has already absorbed that outcome. When a decision is this fully priced, the rate itself stops being the market-moving event. What moves yields and equities instead is the forward guidance: the statement's language, the quarterly Summary of Economic Projections (the 'dot plot'), and Chair Powell's tone in the press conference, because those are the inputs that tell investors what happens at the next meeting, not this one.

Forward guidance works because the Fed's job isn't just to set today's rate, it's to manage the entire expected path of rates, since long-term borrowing costs for mortgages, corporate bonds and credit cards are priced off expectations years out, not off the fed funds rate alone. A 'hawkish hold,' the outcome most analysts expect this month, means the Fed keeps rates unchanged but signals it isn't done tightening if inflation data firms up. That single word choice can move the 2-year yield, which is more sensitive to near-term policy expectations, by several basis points within minutes of the statement's release, well before anyone parses the dot plot in detail.

What a lot of people miss is that the Fed is making this call with an unusually thin data set this cycle. A backlog from earlier-year data disruptions pushed back official releases like the jobs report, forcing policymakers to lean more heavily on private substitutes such as ADP's payroll count. The closest historical parallel is 1996, when Alan Greenspan famously navigated a government shutdown-driven data gap by trusting internal Fed models and anecdotal evidence over hard numbers, and still managed a soft landing. The lesson from that episode is that forward guidance becomes more, not less, important when the underlying data is noisy, because it's the clearest signal the Fed can send when its own inputs are degraded.

For Chris, the practical read-through sits right in today's numbers: a 10-year at 5.12% already prices in a hold, so the trade isn't guessing the rate, it's gauging whether next week's language shifts the probability of a December move. Watch the 2-year yield's reaction in the minutes after the statement drops; a sharp move there, more than any single day's S&P print, is the cleanest tell for whether markets think the Fed just got more or less worried about inflation reaccelerating into year-end.
